job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his sister Meera were watching a documentary about the Olympics. Meera asked, 'Do the Games happen every year?' Rohan shook his head, explaining that the modern Olympic Games occur every four years, unlike the ancient ones which were held in Olympia, not Athens. He pointed to the Olympic rings on the screen, clarifying that the five rings represent the union of the five inhabited continents, not specific founding countries. As the documentary discussed doping, Rohan noted that athletes are strictly responsible for what enters their bodies. Even if a doctor prescribes a medicine, an athlete must check if it is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list; ignorance is no excuse. Meera then asked about the Paralympic Games. Rohan explained that they are a distinct event for athletes with physical impairments, separate from the Special Olympics. He reminded her that the Olympic spirit is not just about winning gold, but about participation and fair play. He mentioned that Abhinav Bindra remains a legend, as his 2008 victory was India’s first individual Olympic gold medal. They both agreed that the dedication required for these sports is immense, regardless of the specific event or the athlete's background, proving that the true value lies in the effort and the spirit of competition.

items.evidence: Rohan shook his head, explaining that the modern Olympic Games occur every four years, unlike the ancient ones which were held in Olympia, not Athens.
items.q: Suppose the modern Olympic Games were held in 2016. Going by Rohan's explanation, when would the next Games be held?
options: In 2020, after a gap of four years
In 2017, after a gap of one year
In 2018, after a gap of two years
In 2024, after a gap of eight years
items.explain: Rohan says the modern Olympic Games happen every four years, so the Games after 2016 come in 2020.

wrong.why: thinks the Olympic Games are held every year
mixes up the gap between Summer and Winter Games
doubles the four-year gap by mistake

items.evidence: He pointed to the Olympic rings on the screen, clarifying that the five rings represent the union of the five inhabited continents, not specific founding countries.
items.q: Why does the Olympic symbol have exactly five rings joined together?
options: They stand for five continents where people live, united
They stand for five countries that founded the Games
They stand for five Games held in ancient Athens
They stand for five sports played at every Games
items.explain: The five rings show the five inhabited continents joined together, not particular founding countries.

wrong.why: thinks each ring stands for a founding country
thinks the ancient Games were held in Athens
guesses the rings stand for events or sports

items.evidence: Even if a doctor prescribes a medicine, an athlete must check if it is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's prohibited list; ignorance is no excuse.
items.q: A doctor gives an athlete a medicine for a cold before a race. What should the athlete do?
options: Check the banned list, since the athlete is responsible
Take it freely, since the doctor is responsible
Take it freely, since not knowing is an excuse
Check the banned list only for very strong medicines
items.explain: Athletes are responsible for everything they take. Even a doctor's medicine must be checked against the prohibited list, because not knowing is no excuse.

wrong.why: thinks the doctor's prescription moves the blame to the doctor
assumes the rule applies only to strong medicines

items.evidence: Rohan explained that they are a distinct event for athletes with physical impairments, separate from the Special Olympics.
items.q: Meera thinks the Paralympics and the Special Olympics are one event. What should Rohan tell her?
options: They are two separate events, not the same one
They are one event known by two different names
They are one event held inside the main Olympics
They are two events, and both are open to everyone
items.explain: Rohan says the Paralympics are a distinct event for athletes with physical impairments, separate from the Special Olympics.

wrong.why: thinks the Paralympics and Special Olympics are the same
thinks the Paralympics are just part of the Olympics
misses that the Paralympics are for athletes with physical impairments

items.evidence: He mentioned that Abhinav Bindra remains a legend, as his 2008 victory was India’s first individual Olympic gold medal.
items.q: Why is Abhinav Bindra's 2008 win remembered as special in India's Olympic history?
options: It was India's first gold won by one person alone
It was India's first Olympic gold of any kind
It was India's first Olympic medal of any kind
It was India's first gold won by a whole team
items.explain: Bindra's 2008 win was India's first individual Olympic gold, meaning the first gold won by one athlete rather than a team.

wrong.why: thinks Bindra won India's first Olympic gold of any kind
confuses which medal came first for India
mixes up individual and team medals
